flashcard_questions.q: What is the theoretical yield of a reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: The maximum mass of product calculated from the balanced equation.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the actual yield of a reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: The mass of product collected at the end of the experiment.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the percentage yield of a reaction?
Why does a reversible reaction give a percentage yield below 100%?
flashcard_questions.a: Not all of the reactants are converted into products.

flashcard_questions.q: A student expected 495 tonnes but obtained 400 tonnes. What is the percentage yield?
What does atom economy measure about a reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: How much of the total mass of the reactants ends up as the useful product.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the atom economy of a reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: (Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of all reactants) × 100

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of reaction has an atom economy of 100%?
flashcard_questions.a: One that makes only a single product, such as an addition reaction.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does industry prefer a reaction with a high atom economy?
flashcard_questions.a: Less waste is produced, so the process is more sustainable and more cost-effective.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the concentration of a solution in mol/dm³?
flashcard_questions.a: moles of solute ÷ volume of solution in dm³

flashcard_questions.q: How many cm³ are there in one dm³?
What is the concentration when 0.5 mol is dissolved in 250 cm³ of solution?
What volume does one mole of any gas occupy at room temperature and pressure?
flashcard_questions.a: 24 dm³, which is the same as 24,000 cm³

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the volume of a gas at room temperature and pressure?
How does percentage yield differ from atom economy?
flashcard_questions.a: Yield shows how well the reaction was carried out; atom economy shows how wasteful its design is.

notes: 15 cards: 4 equation cards quoted verbatim (percentage yield, atom economy, concentration, gas volume), 4 term→definition (theoretical yield, actual yield, atom economy, molar volume), 3 worked value answers (80.8%, 2 mol/dm³, 1000 cm³ per dm³), 4 explanation cards including the yield-versus-atom-economy distinction. Dropped transfer losses and side reactions as separate yield-loss cards, and the 168 dm³ worked answer, to stay inside 15 and avoid a run of near-identical calculation cards.
